feature_overview.business_goal: Deliver the Task Search feature for the SaaS application.
scope: Implement search functionality for tasks by keyword in title or description
Display matching tasks as a list with links to task detail pages
Support real-time search as user types
out_of_scope: Search across multiple projects or workspaces
Search in task comments or tags
Full-text search with natural language processing
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Task Search feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: Search tasks by keyword in their title or description, showing matching tasks as a list with links to each task's detail page.

acceptance_criteria.description: When a user enters a keyword, matching tasks are displayed in a list with links to their detail pages.
Search is case-insensitive and returns results from both title and description fields.
Search results load within 2 seconds for up to 1000 tasks.

validation_rules.description: Search keyword must be at least 2 characters long to initiate search.

non_functional_requirements.description: Search results should load within 2 seconds for up to 1000 tasks.
The search feature must support case-insensitive matching.

architecture_approach.architecture_rationale: Use modular to keep the Task Search feature separated into presentation, business logic, and data responsibilities where applicable.
architecture_approach.frontend_overview: Frontend design should provide the user-facing entry points, inputs, states, and feedback required by the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.backend_overview: Backend design should process feature requests, enforce business rules, validate inputs, and return structured responses.
architecture_approach.data_overview: Data design should support the data requirements defined in the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.integration_overview: Integration design should follow the API expectations and dependencies listed in the approved SRS.
design_tradeoffs: Design is derived directly from the approved SRS to preserve traceability and feature scope.
Design is kept feature-scoped to preserve feature-by-feature SDLC development.
Internal generation or repair details are kept in backend logs and are not exposed in the approval-ready Architecture Plan.
